accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core RL.1.7 (use illustrations and details to describe characters, setting or events), RI.1.6 (information from pictures versus words), RL.3.7 (illustrations create mood and emphasise setting) and RI.2.7 (images clarify a text). Rosie's Walk is correctly described: the text never names the fox, who appears only in the illustrations.

misconceptions.evidence: Wrong moves name real slips: assuming the picture just repeats the words (the predict and the Words/Picture/Both sort), choosing a picture that contradicts the text (a moon for 'a sunny day'), thinking the words alone set the feeling, missing the fox, and calling a one-word label a caption. The adult text warns against covering pictures to make a child 'really read'.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpic combines a three-bin fact sort, sticker illustration of sentences, sky/weather/face toggles that change mood under fixed words, a three-page fox hunt and a bee diagram with labels and a caption. flagbook labels physical book parts (cover, spine, blurb) and flagwread is phonics; none relates picture to text. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Placing a moon on 'a sunny day' is rejected with a reason ('A moon means night, but the words say a sunny day.'), and on the mood step the child must flip the same page from scary back to happy, so they see three picture choices, not the words, carry the feeling.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions: whether a picture can tell more than the words (tempting answer: no, it copies them), whether a dark stormy picture leaves the story feeling the same, and whether Hen is the only one in the story. Each is tested immediately by its step and quoted in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions (snow only in the picture, sunny-day match, bright versus dark mood, the fox in Rosie's Walk, label versus caption) with tagged wrong answers: words-only, picture contradicts text, words decide mood, fox is Hen, title not caption. Each tag returns a one-line correction.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK 1.2 against the family limit of 5.0 with short quoted examples ('Max the dog wants to play.'). Adult text scores FK 9.5 against 10 and uses illustration, illustrator, caption, label, diagram, mood, setting and the match/extend/counterpoint picturebook terms.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph pairs a rule with a concrete page (Max in the rain, Mia in the woods, Hen and the fox, a bee diagram), and the adult paragraphs give standards, picturebook theory, named mistakes and the lab sequence; overlap with other lessons is under 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: 360x640 shots in light and dark show the picture panel above the sentence, tap targets of at least 44 px for the three bins and four stickers, and the three mood toggles plus Done wrapping into two rows below the canvas with nothing clipped. Every Show me completed on iPhone 13 within the limit.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop and iPhone and there were no console errors. Every canvas target has a labelled button twin (bins, stickers, Sky/Weather/Mia toggles that state their current value, Hen/A fox/The haystack, bee parts, caption choices) and feedback is spoken via the aria-label.

sources: Common Core State Standards ELA RL.1.7, RI.1.6, RI.2.7, RL.3.7
